Drug product manufacturing information.
Name, address, and responsibility of each drug product manufacturer.
Batch formula for manufacturing the drug product at the proposed batch size.

text: 3.2.P.3.3 — Description of Manufacturing Process and Process Controls
desc: Drug product manufacturing process description with flow diagram and process controls.

text: 3.2.P.3.4 — Controls of Critical Steps and Intermediates
desc: In-process controls and tests for critical manufacturing steps and intermediates.
Drug product process validation studies and evaluation results.
Quality control information for excipients used in the drug product formulation.
Specifications for excipients including tests and acceptance criteria.
Analytical procedures used for excipient testing.
Validation of analytical methods used for excipient testing.
Justification for excipient specifications and acceptance criteria.

text: 3.2.P.4.5 — Excipients of Human or Animal Origin
desc: Information on excipients derived from human or animal sources, including adventitious agent safety.
Full details on novel excipients not previously used in approved drug products.
Drug product quality control including specifications, analytical procedures, and batch data.
Drug product release and shelf-life specifications with tests and acceptance criteria.
Detailed analytical procedures used for drug product testing.
Validation reports for drug product analytical methods.
Certificate of analysis and batch analytical results for representative drug product batches.
Identification, qualification, and characterization of drug product impurities and degradation products.
Justification for the proposed drug product specifications and acceptance criteria.
Information on reference standards and reference materials used for drug product testing.
Description and specifications for the drug product container closure system, including suitability studies.
Drug product stability data, conclusions, and post-approval protocols.
Summary of drug product stability studies and conclusions supporting the proposed shelf life.

desc: Post-approval stability protocol for ongoing monitoring and stability commitment.
Detailed drug product stability study data under long-term, accelerated, and stress conditions.
Quality appendices covering facilities, adventitious agents, and novel excipients.
Detailed information on manufacturing facilities and major equipment.
Detailed adventitious agents safety evaluation for biological/biotechnology-derived products.
Full CMC details for novel excipients not previously approved, provided in drug substance format.
Region-specific quality information (e.g., executed batch records, comparability protocols, methods validation packages).

Nonclinical (preclinical) study reports covering pharmacology, pharmacokinetics, and toxicology. In v4.0, study reports are stored flat under 4.2 with section placement via Context of Use codes.
All nonclinical study reports. Physical storage is flat ({study-id}/ folders directly under 42-stud-rep/); the CoU code determines TOC section placement.
Nonclinical pharmacology studies evaluating the pharmacological activity and mechanism of action of the drug.
Studies evaluating the primary pharmacological effect of the drug related to its intended therapeutic indication.
Studies evaluating pharmacological effects of the drug not related to the desired therapeutic effect.
Studies evaluating potential undesirable pharmacological effects on physiological functions (cardiovascular, CNS, respiratory per ICH S7A/S7B).
Nonclinical studies evaluating pharmacodynamic interactions between the drug and other substances.
Nonclinical pharmacokinetic studies characterizing ADME properties and drug interactions.
Reports on bioanalytical methods and their validation for nonclinical PK studies.
Nonclinical absorption studies including bioavailability, rate and extent of absorption.
Nonclinical distribution studies including tissue distribution, protein binding, and placental transfer.
Nonclinical metabolism studies including metabolite identification, metabolic pathways, and enzyme induction/inhibition.
Nonclinical excretion studies including routes and rates of elimination, mass balance studies.
Nonclinical studies evaluating pharmacokinetic drug-drug interactions.
Other nonclinical PK studies not covered by the above categories.
Nonclinical toxicology studies evaluating the safety profile of the drug. Keywords for species and route of administration are required for many sub-sections.
Acute (single-dose) toxicity studies. Required keywords: study id, species, route of administration.
Repeat-dose (subacute, subchronic, chronic) toxicity studies. Required keywords: study id, species, route of administration. Optional: duration.
Genotoxicity studies evaluating potential mutagenic and clastogenic activity.
In vitro genotoxicity studies (e.g., Ames test, chromosomal aberration, mouse lymphoma assay).
In vivo genotoxicity studies (e.g., micronucleus, comet assay, transgenic rodent models).
Carcinogenicity studies evaluating tumorigenic potential.
Long-term (2-year) carcinogenicity studies. Required keyword: species.
Short or medium-term carcinogenicity studies (e.g., 6-month transgenic mouse models).
Other carcinogenicity-related studies not classified as long-term or short/medium-term.
Studies evaluating effects on fertility, embryofetal development, and pre/postnatal development per ICH S5.
Studies evaluating effects on male and female fertility and early embryonic development (ICH S5 Segment I).
Embryo-fetal development studies evaluating teratogenic potential (ICH S5 Segment II).

text: 4.2.3.5.3 — Prenatal and Postnatal Development, Including Maternal Function
desc: Pre- and postnatal development studies evaluating effects on offspring and maternal function (ICH S5 Segment III).

text: 4.2.3.5.4 — Studies in Which the Offspring (Juvenile Animals) Are Dosed and/or Further Evaluated
desc: Juvenile animal toxicity studies where offspring are directly dosed or further evaluated.
Local tolerance studies evaluating irritation and sensitization at the site of drug application.
Other toxicity studies not covered by the standard ICH categories.
Studies evaluating the antigenic potential of the drug substance.
Studies evaluating effects on the immune system per ICH S8 guidelines.
Mechanistic studies to understand specific toxicological findings observed in other studies.
Nonclinical dependence and abuse liability studies.
Toxicity studies on disproportionate or unique human metabolites per ICH M3(R2)/MIST guidance.
Toxicity studies on drug substance or drug product impurities per ICH Q3A/Q3B.
Other toxicity studies not classified elsewhere (e.g., phototoxicity, combination toxicity).
Published literature references cited in Module 4 nonclinical study reports.
Clinical study reports and related information. In v4.0, study reports are stored flat under 5.3 with section placement via Context of Use codes.

text: 5.2 — Tabular Listing of All Clinical Studies

text: 5.3 — Clinical Study Reports and Related Information
desc: All clinical study reports organized by study type. Physical storage is flat ({study-id}/ folders directly under 53-clin-stud-rep/); the CoU code determines TOC section placement.
Biopharmaceutic studies including bioavailability, bioequivalence, in vitro-in vivo correlation, and bioanalytical methods.
Bioavailability study reports and related information.

text: 5.3.1.2 — Comparative BA and Bioequivalence (BE) Study Reports
desc: Comparative bioavailability and bioequivalence study reports (e.g., food effect, formulation comparison).

desc: Reports establishing correlation between in vitro dissolution and in vivo bioavailability.

text: 5.3.1.4 — Reports of Bioanalytical and Analytical Methods for Human Studies
desc: Validation reports for bioanalytical and analytical methods used in clinical studies.

text: 5.3.2 — Reports of Studies Pertinent to PK Using Human Biomaterials
desc: In vitro studies using human biomaterials to characterize PK properties (plasma protein binding, hepatic metabolism, drug interactions).

text: 5.3.2.2 — Reports of Hepatic Metabolism and Drug Interaction Studies
desc: In vitro hepatic metabolism studies including CYP enzyme identification and inhibition/induction potential.

text: 5.3.2.3 — Reports of Studies Using Other Human Biomaterials
desc: Studies using other human biomaterials not covered by plasma protein binding or hepatic metabolism.
Clinical pharmacokinetic studies in healthy subjects and patients.

text: 5.3.3.1 — Healthy Subject PK and Initial Tolerability Study Reports
desc: PK and tolerability studies in healthy volunteers (Phase 1 first-in-human, single/multiple ascending dose).

text: 5.3.3.2 — Patient PK and Initial Tolerability Study Reports
desc: PK and tolerability studies conducted in the target patient population.
PK studies evaluating the effect of intrinsic factors (age, sex, race, weight, renal/hepatic impairment, genetic polymorphism).
PK studies evaluating the effect of extrinsic factors (food, drugs, smoking, etc.) on pharmacokinetics.
Population pharmacokinetic analyses and modeling reports.
Clinical pharmacodynamic and PK/PD studies.

text: 5.3.4.1 — Healthy Subject PD and PK/PD Study Reports
desc: Pharmacodynamic and PK/PD relationship studies in healthy volunteers.

text: 5.3.4.2 — Patient PD and PK/PD Study Reports
desc: Pharmacodynamic and PK/PD relationship studies in the target patient population.

text: 5.3.5 — Reports of Efficacy and Safety Studies
desc: Pivotal and supportive efficacy/safety clinical studies. Required keyword: indication.

desc: Reports of controlled clinical studies (randomized, blinded, etc.) supporting the claimed indication. Required keyword: type of control.

text: 5.3.5.2 — Study Reports of Uncontrolled Clinical Studies
desc: Reports of uncontrolled clinical studies (open-label, single-arm) supporting the claimed indication.

desc: Integrated analyses across multiple studies including Integrated Summary of Safety (ISS) and Integrated Summary of Efficacy (ISE).
Other clinical study reports including antibacterial/antiviral microbiology, BIMO inspections, human factors validation, and special pathogen studies.
Postmarketing safety experience reports including periodic adverse drug experience reports (PADERs).
